title: Inverse derivative of the exponential map as Bernoulli-adjoint series (dexpinv / Magnus)
expression_sketch:
Lie-group / Magnus setup (Iserles-Munthe-Kaas-Norsett-Zanna, Acta Numerica 2000, (2.40)-(2.46) and (4.3)). For a C^1 curve Omega(t) in a matrix Lie algebra,
  d/dt exp(Omega) = dexp_{Omega}(Omega') * exp(Omega)   (right-trivialised convention; left analogue likewise),
  dexp_Omega(H) = Sum_{k>=0} ad_Omega^k (H) / (k+1)!  = Integral(exp(s*ad_Omega)(H), (s, 0, 1)),
  dexp_Omega^{-1}(H) = Sum_{k>=0} (B_k / k!) ad_Omega^k (H),
where ad_Omega(H) = Omega*H - H*Omega, ad^0 = Id, and B_k are Bernoulli numbers generated by
  w / (exp(w)-1) = Sum_{k>=0} B_k w^k / k!    for |w| < 2*pi,
  B0=1, B1=-1/2, B2=1/6, B3=0, B4=-1/30.
Truncation: dexp^{-1}(H) = H - (1/2)[Omega,H] + (1/12)[Omega,[Omega,H]] + ...
Magnus ODE: Omega' = dexp_Omega^{-1}(A(t)), Omega(0)=0, recovers Y'=A(t)Y via Y=exp(Omega).
Scalar commuting probe (SymPy): ad=0 so dexp_w(h)=h, but the generating-function member is
  (exp(w)-1)/w * (w/(exp(w)-1)) == 1  (entire continuation, value 1 at 0).
latent_structure: Master object: the adjoint representation ad_Omega together with the Bernoulli generating function w/(e^w-1). The forward dexp (integral / phi_1(ad) series), its inverse (Bernoulli-ad series), and the Magnus generator Omega' are three operators on that pair. This is the inverse of the Frechet derivative of exp, not the Van Loan 2-block packaging of that Frechet derivative.

function_domains.B_k: Bernoulli numbers, B_k = B_k(0), generating function w/(exp(w)-1) for |w|<2*pi
function_domains.ad_Omega: commutator representation; polynomial (entire) in the entries of Omega and H

nonzero_conditions.statement: dexp_Omega is invertible iff spec(ad_Omega) avoids 2*pi*I*Z \ {0}, i.e. no pair of eigenvalues of Omega differs by 2*pi*I*m for integer m != 0
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Iserles, Munthe-Kaas, Norsett and Zanna, Acta Numerica 9 (2000) 215-365, discussion of dexp^{-1}; Hairer, Lubich and Wanner, Geometric Numerical Integration, 2ed, Sec. IV.7; equivalent spectral condition for the Frechet derivative of exp (Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Sec. 10.2)

positivity_conditions.statement: Integral parameter s ranges over the compact interval [0, 1]
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: Iserles et al., Acta Numerica 9 (2000), integral form of dexp; Hairer-Lubich-Wanner, GNI 2ed, IV.7

analytic_domains.statement: Bernoulli generating function w/(exp(w)-1) is holomorphic on the disk |w| < 2*pi (simple poles of exp(w)-1 at 2*pi*I*Z \ {0})
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Abramowitz and Stegun, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, eq. 23.1.1; Iserles et al., Acta Numerica 9 (2000)

analytic_domains.statement: The integral form dexp_Omega(H) = Integral(exp(s ad_Omega)(H), (s,0,1)) is an entire function of the entries (finite-dimensional matrices; no cut)
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Iserles et al., Acta Numerica 9 (2000), (2.40)-(2.46); Hairer-Lubich-Wanner, GNI IV.7

branch_conventions: Primary matrix exponential in exp(s ad_Omega); ad_Omega acts on matrices, not an entrywise exponential.
w/(exp(w)-1) denotes the entire continuation of the generating function through w=0 (value 1).

limit_domains.statement: w -> 0 unrestricted in C for the scalar generating-function identity; s in [0,1] compact
limit_domains.label: DECLARED

source_provenance: Iserles, Munthe-Kaas, Norsett, Zanna, Lie-group methods, Acta Numerica 9 (2000) 215-365, eqs. (2.40)-(2.46), (4.3)
Hairer, Lubich, Wanner, Geometric Numerical Integration, 2ed, Springer, Sec. IV.7
Hausdorff, Ber. Verh. Kgl. Sachs. Ges. Wiss. Leipzig 58 (1906) 19-48

derived_conditions.statement: On the disk |w|<2*pi the product ((exp(w)-1)/w) * (w/(exp(w)-1)) equals 1, so the scalar commuting reduction of dexp o dexp^{-1} is the identity
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Bernoulli generating function vs. the series of (exp(w)-1)/w; Iserles et al. inversion of dexp

derived_conditions.statement: B3=0 and all odd B_k=0 for k>=3 follow from w/(e^w-1) + w/2 being even
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED

public_source: Iserles, Munthe-Kaas, Norsett and Zanna, Lie-group methods, Acta Numerica 9 (2000) 215-365, eqs. (2.40)-(2.46) and (4.3), doi:10.1017/S0962492900002154; Magnus, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 7 (1954) 649-673; Hairer, Lubich and Wanner, Geometric Numerical Integration, 2ed, Sec. IV.7.
why_not_cse_lgg: CSE will not invent Bernoulli numbers or the adjoint tower ad^k. The Van Loan Duhamel integral is the forward Frechet, not its inverse. LGG has no ad-series constructor. Distinct from historical sciml-vanloan-blockexp-01 and sciml-adjoint-linear-01 (Pontryagin adjoint of an ODE, not dexpinv).
proposer_leak_risk: Hide: dexp, dexpinv, Magnus, Bernoulli, adjoint representation, Lie algebra, Hausdorff, Van Loan, Frechet, phi. Show the unlabeled series H - (1/2)[O,H] + (1/12)[O,[O,H]] and the scalar pair (exp(w)-1)/w , w/(exp(w)-1).
notes: SciML role: geometric integration, RKMK / Magnus integrators, autodiff of Lie-group exponential maps (SO(3)/SE(3) nets). Catalog: G0001=(exp(w)-1)/w; G0002=w/(exp(w)-1); G0003=1; G0004=H - (1/2)*(O*H-H*O). F = (ad, Bernoulli generating function). NOT the Van Loan block and NOT phi_k = exp[0^{(k)}, z].
